topics.topic: Decide whether resolved photo-folder checks occur during startup whole-file validation or per operation
questions: Does a record break rule 8 at startup only when its subfolder strings violate the lexical restrictions, or also when the current filesystem resolution of its photo folder is not strictly below the root?
Is the resolved-photo-folder condition part of whole-file startup validation, or is it checked only for the requested project during scan and placement?

Does a record break rule 8 at startup when its syntactically valid photo subfolder is missing, is not a directory, or resolves outside the root, even though rule 8 requires those resolved-path checks only "On each scan and placement"?

quotes:
Each scan, placement and mark reads the connections file exactly once, at its connection check,
   and uses that reading for the whole operation. A change written later applies from the next
   operation without a restart, and an operation that has already read the file finishes on that
   reading. The file is judged whole before any project is looked up, so the first condition that
   applies decides:
| 1 | the file is absent or cannot be read, is not UTF-8 or valid JSON, does not have the record form, or any record breaks rule 8 | `folder_unavailable` |
The service does not start when condition 1 applies.

The photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without `..` and are not the root
   itself. On each scan and placement
   the photo folder must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused
   with `folder_unavailable`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats failed resolved-photo-folder containment as a record breaking rule 8 and refuses startup; another validates only the lexical record form at startup and performs resolved containment only for the requested scan or placement, which the operator and calling flow observe as startup failure versus a running service.
judgement.why: The reference to any record breaking rule 8 does not say whether it includes the condition expressly introduced as applying on each scan and placement.

The service starts and the valid project scans successfully because resolved containment is checked only when its project is scanned or placed.

precedent.topic: Authoritative camera timestamp, timezone interpretation, and fallback criteria
quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
precedent.why: A2 specifies field precedence, offset handling, the configured-zone interpretation, ambiguous and nonexistent local times, and every fallback criterion.
